src/infrastructure/app.ts: GET /orders calls `orderService.getOrdersByState(state as any)`, so the state value's type is never checked

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module has two files with one concern, the HTTP entry point. app.ts's createApp() builds the services and maps the HTTP routes onto OrderService and CatalogueService. index.ts only starts the server. Each handler hands its work to the services rather than reimplementing order or catalogue logic, so no business rule is copied here. Smaller issues: (1) three handlers each repeat the same try/catch that turns an error into a 400 response; this is boilerplate rather than a duplicated domain rule, and one shared error handler could replace it. (2) GET /orders passes the state query value through 'state as any', so its type is never checked; the type belongs to another module, so this isn't a bypass of this module's own abstractions. (3) createApp seeds sample products, which mixes demo data into setup code but is still part of setting up the app. None of these reaches the rubric's failure threshold.
